subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + next steps
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + next steps

Hi Samantha and Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion and helpful context on your high-volume chat flows and the strict latency targets for search-assist (sub-150ms for most queries). Per our demo and the evals we ran against your prompt set, I put together a shortlist of recommended models with rationale and tradeoffs.

Recommended shortlist (POC stage):
- redwood-13B-instruct-8k-quant
  - Why: best balance of cost and 95th-percentile latency for token-limited chat use (low memory footprint, good instruction-following).
  - Tradeoffs: slightly higher hallucination rate on extremely rare domain-specific prompts vs larger models; we mitigated with prompt templates and deterministic decoding in the evals.
- redwood-70B-instruct-8k (float16)
  - Why: top quality on the ACME prompt set (lowest semantic error and fewer follow-up clarifications).
  - Tradeoffs: ~2.8x higher cost and ~1.8x higher median latency compared to the 13B quant variant. Good for high-value tasks where accuracy is paramount.
- open-llama-30B-8k (baseline)
  - Why: useful as a low-cost fallback and for throughput-heavy batch reranking.
  - Tradeoffs: lower instruction adherence in a few templates; acceptable for non-customer-facing batch jobs.

Quick benchmark highlights (summary):
- 13B-quant: median latency ~85ms (p95 ~140ms), cost estimate (tokens) ~$0.0009 per request on POC traffic profile.
- 70B: median latency ~160ms (p95 ~290ms), cost estimate ~$0.0026 per request.
- Open-30B: median latency ~120ms, cost estimate ~$0.0014 per request.

I've attached the ACME prompt set we used (acme_prompt_set_v1.json) and a one-page benchmarks summary (acme_benchmarks_summary.pdf). Full raw logs and perf traces are in the Drive link below.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm which model you want for the POC (suggestion: redwood-13B-instruct-8k-quant to start).
2) We prepare a 4-week mutual action plan (POC objectives, success metrics, data access).
3) Schedule a follow-up sync next week to finalize scope and pricing.

Suggested times: Tue 2026-06-23 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 2026-06-24 14:00-15:00 PT.

If you want, we can also include a brief A/B run of 13B vs 70B for a small set of high-value queries to help quantify UX delta.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Samantha —

Great questions. Short answers first, then data: 
- Hallucination/precision on "product_description" bucket (top-line): 13B-quant false-positive rate ~6.8% (we defined FP as asserting non-existent SKU attributes). 70B: ~2.1%. We included a small prompt-template change that reduces hallucination on 13B to ~4.5% at the cost of slightly longer responses. Full per-prompt breakdown is in the Drive link and the attached benchmarks summary.
- Latency numbers are steady-state under a simulated production QPS profile matching the volumes you shared (includes warmed KV cache). For burst cold-starts (new worker spin-ups) expect higher p95; we recommend using a small warm pool in Dedicated or pin instances for Private to keep p95 under your 150ms target.

Mitigations we recommend if you start with 13B-quant:
- Apply the "SKU-safe" prompt wrapper (included in acme_prompt_set_v1.json) to force verification steps when model is unsure.
- Function/tool-calling pattern for SKU lookup: try deterministic model-first check + system-of-record fallback (we can add that wiring in the POC).
- Lightweight reranker (open-llama-30B) for top-5 outputs in high-value flows to reduce FP in final candidate.

Pricing & POC plan: I've attached a one-page mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_acme.docx) with milestones and a preliminary pricing estimate for a 4-week POC using redwood-13B-instruct-8k-quant.

If that sounds good I'll schedule the kickoff for Tue 2026-06-23 at 10:00 PT (suggested).

Cheers,
Marissa
